oracle.query_domain_description: Each operation's query_signature is the authoritative query domain. Permissions for queries outside the ball or restrictions to feasible queries are enforced separately for each interface.
description_paragraphs: Public inputs include the block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $\Delta$, $G_0$, $\beta$, $\beta_{\rm ms}$, $\varepsilon$, $\mu_y$, and $\sigma$. The stated initial points and feasible-set information are also supplied. An analytic representation of the hidden function, operator, or matrix is not revealed.

Sample identifiers $\xi$ are drawn independently from an unknown distribution fixed before interaction. Identifiers may be stored and used to evaluate $\nabla f_\xi$ at several points in the full space. Every sample–point evaluation is charged.

A paired-sample difference at two points requires two evaluations. Values and Hessians are unavailable. Adaptive points chosen after obtaining a reusable sample identifier need not be unbiased conditional on the entire history; fixed-point unbiasedness and persistent sample coupling retain their model definitions.

objects.definition: The unknown distribution of sample functions is fixed before interaction. After independently drawing identifier $\xi$, that identifier refers to the same $f_\xi$ at every query point.
A fixed sample identifier $\xi$ specifies a differentiable function $f_\xi:\mathbb R^{d_x+d_y}\to\mathbb R$. The population objective is $f=\mathbb E_\xi f_\xi$.
The feasible set is explicitly public. Exact projections and linear algebra use known geometry and reveal no hidden-function information.

norms.definition: The Euclidean norm and inner product are $\|v\|_2=(\sum_jv_j^2)^{1/2}$ and $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j u_jv_j$. On the joint space use $\|(x,y)\|_2=(\|x\|_2^2+\|y\|_2^2)^{1/2}$.
